name: forma
description: Turn a screenshot, a PDF, or an existing report into a real DevExpress .repx — AI-generated spec, in-browser mockup, and XtraReports XML. Bring your own Gemini key.
comment:pdfjs-dist: The floor is ^6.5.438 on purpose (2026-11-12, owner decision 18 of the 2026-11-11 audit). GHSA-hq66-cqwq-w95j (high: arbitrary JavaScript execution upon opening a malicious PDF) affects >=5.6.83 <6.2.108, and every PDF a person attaches is opened with pdf.js in the browser, so the range must never admit a version below 6.2.108: do not lower this floor, and never write a range that reaches back into 5.x. The 5.x line was pinned to exactly 5.5.207 that morning after an in-range update went to 5.7.284, inside the advisory; the move to 6 removed the pin. What 6.x changed for this project was only in the tests: a document is released with `loadingTask.destroy()` (src/lib/pdf.ts already did), `isEvalSupported` is gone because 6.x evaluates no code, and `getPermissions()` answers a Set. `npm audit` and the PDF tests (pdf, pdfA, pdfCrypto, pdfWriter, repxIntake) are the checks; the two pdfjs chunks have budgets in scripts/check-bundle-size.mjs.
comment:overrides: qs: two Dependabot advisories (array-limit bypass, DoS via attacker-controlled isBuffer) are fixed in 6.16.0. Until 2026-11-12 the consumer that settled it was this project's own express@4, whose ~6.15.1 could only resolve to an affected version; since then (owner decision 18) this project's express is 5.3.0, which asks for ^6.16.0 itself. Two consumers inside firebase-tools still declare ranges that admit an affected version, exegesis (^6.6.0) and googleapis-common (^6.7.0), and the express@4 nested in firebase-tools asks for ~6.16.0, which does not. `npm audit fix` cannot lift them without a breaking change, so the override pins every copy instead. Every qs in the tree was already 6.x, so this is a patch-level lift, not a major. body-parser 2.4.0 asks for ^6.16.1, a floor above this override's, but 6.16.1 is what resolves, so nothing is lowered in practice. Remove this entry once no consumer's own range admits a version below 6.16.0. `npm explain qs` is the check: it prints each consumer as overridden ... (was <its own range>). `npm ls qs --all` cannot answer it, because it shows versions after the override has been applied. sharp (2026-11-06): three high Dependabot advisories, in the librsvg, libheif and libvips it bundles, are fixed in 0.35.5, and its only consumer, @huggingface/transformers, asked for ^0.34.1 in every 3.x release. transformers is 4.3.2 since 2026-11-12, which asks for ^0.35.4: that still admits 0.35.4, an affected version, so the override stays until a release asks for 0.35.5 or later, the rule the qs entry follows. A 0.34 to 0.35 move is semver-major for a 0.x package, and it is safe here for a reason qs did not need: nothing ships sharp. Forma imports Transformers.js only in the browser (src/lib/handwriting.ts), where the package resolves to dist/transformers.web.js, which does not import sharp, and nothing that runs under Node imports Transformers.js at all. The one thing that loads sharp is scripts/make-icons.mjs, run by hand under Node to draw the icons, and it takes whichever sharp this override settles. Its install script is denied in allowScripts below, so for everything the build and the tests do, the override changes only which files sit in node_modules. It was checked anyway, on 2026-11-06: under Node, Transformers.js 3.7.6 still read an image through sharp 0.35.5 (RawImage.read, with the install script denied). Remove this entry when @huggingface/transformers asks for 0.35.5 or later, not merely a range that includes it; `npm explain sharp` is the check, as for qs.
comment:not-overridden: What npm audit still reports is deliberately NOT overridden, and none of it ships: every flagged package is Firestore's Node.js transport or a part of firebase-tools, and dist/ holds neither. @grpc/grpc-js (high, fixed in 1.13.6) is pinned ~1.9.0 by @firebase/firestore, still so in 4.20.0, firebase 13.3.0's, on 2026-11-12, so no firebase release fixes it, and an override would push another package's internals four minors past the range it asked for. The browser entry never imports it, so here it runs only in the rules tests, against the local emulator; it is also the whole reason firebase, both Firestore packages and @firebase/rules-unit-testing are flagged high. Recheck when a firebase release's Firestore asks for @grpc/grpc-js 1.13.6 or later: `npm view @firebase/firestore@latest dependencies.@grpc/grpc-js`. The rest live inside firebase-tools, which runs the emulator and nothing else here: uuid via gaxios, @opentelemetry/core via @google-cloud/pubsub, and minimatch 9, which glob 10 asks for, glob 10 coming in through firebase-tools itself and through archiver, exegesis and rimraf; the packages between them are flagged only for carrying those. Each fix is a major past what its consumer asks for, and firebase-tools 15.35.0, the latest on 2026-11-11, still asks for glob ^10.5.0 and the same gaxios, google-auth-library and @google-cloud/pubsub ranges, so the fixes have to come from upstream. Recheck after each firebase-tools release with `npm audit` and `npm ls @grpc/grpc-js uuid @opentelemetry/core minimatch glob --all`. Only firebase-tools' own in-range fixes are taken: that is how csv-parse and stream-json closed. firebase stayed at 12.12.1 from 2026-11-04, when `npm audit fix` moved it to 12.19.0 within its range, which fixed no advisory and grew the Firestore chunk every signed-in visitor downloads from under 478,000 bytes to 668,704, so it was put back. It is 13.3.0 since 2026-11-12 by the owner's choice (decision 18 of the 2026-11-11 audit), made with the measurement in hand: no advisory fixed, the auth chunk +3,388 bytes, and the Firestore chunk 346,913 -> 584,217 (+237,304), 149,959 of it re2js, a regular-expression engine Firestore 4.20 now imports, and the rest Firestore's own growth. @firebase/rules-unit-testing went to 6.0.0 with it, which asks for Node 24.12 or later, so `npm run test:rules` does (CI's rules job runs on 24). Forcing a major into firebase-tools is a different proposition from the patch-level qs lift above, because it runs the Firestore emulator that `npm run test:rules` depends on, and breaking it takes the whole rules suite with it. Leave the alerts OPEN rather than dismissing them: an open alert closes itself when upstream bumps its dependencies, a dismissed one stays silent forever. minimatch's #53 is left open on that reasoning. The owner's account dismissed @grpc/grpc-js's #45 and #46 and uuid's #1 as not used on 2026-10-28, each with its reason written on the alert, and Dependabot auto-dismissed @opentelemetry/core's #2, a development dependency, on 2026-09-09; those will not close or reappear on their own when upstream fixes them, so npm audit and the commands above are where they show.
comment:allowScripts: Four approvals pinned to a version and three denials pinned to none. npm 11.19 warns on every install about dependencies whose install scripts nobody has reviewed. The approvals, esbuild 0.28.2, protobufjs 7.6.6 and re2 1.26.1, were reviewed and approved on 2026-10-24, and all of them had already been running on every install; @firebase/util was approved at 1.15.0 then, and at 1.15.3 on 2026-11-12 when firebase 13 brought it (owner decision 18), its postinstall.js read again and found the same: it acts only when FIREBASE_WEBAPP_CONFIG is set, and otherwise writes dist/postinstall.js and .mjs exporting no defaults. esbuild 0.25.12, approved with them, left with Vite 6: Vite 8 uses this project's own 0.28.2, so its entry went too. re2 is the only one doing real work: node-gyp compiles its native binding, an optional dependency of superstatic inside firebase-tools. esbuild verifies its platform binary. protobufjs only prints a version-scheme warning, and @firebase/util only acts when FIREBASE_WEBAPP_CONFIG is set, which App Hosting uses and this project does not. Approvals are pinned to versions, npm's default, so a script whose code changes gets reviewed again: a bump to an approved package brings the warning back on purpose. The three denials carry no version, so each covers every version and a bump never brings one back. After an update, `npm install-scripts ls` names what needs approving and `npm install-scripts prune` drops entries no longer installed. Its --dry-run flag wrote this block anyway on npm 11.19.0, so do not rely on it to preview. tesseract.js (OCR, 2026-11-01) is reviewed and DENIED, for every version: its postinstall is opencollective-postinstall, which only prints a funding message, and nothing it does is needed; the engine's files are copied at build by vite.config.ts instead. onnxruntime-node and sharp (handwriting, 2026-11-04) are reviewed and DENIED, for every version: both arrive with @huggingface/transformers for Node, onnxruntime-node's postinstall fetches native and GPU binaries and sharp's checks or builds its image library, and Forma runs Transformers.js only in the browser, on onnxruntime-web, where neither is used. Since 2026-11-10 onnxruntime-node is also a devDependency, imported by the measuring scripts (scripts/model/paddleOcr.ts) on the CPU binaries its package ships for every platform: the denied postinstall only downloads the Linux CUDA ones, so nothing they need is lost.
